Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> blackday wrote:

> blackday wrote:
> erebus mask

Requires: Harbinger of Skulls
The Harbinger of Skulls with this equipment gets +1 stealth.

It does not even implicitly require a sect to play, because the relevant Harbinger of Skulls could be of any sect - Camarilla, Laibon, Independent, Sabbat, or any other sect that might be invented.

> blackday wrote:
> sword of judgement?
>
Sword of Judgment doesn't require a sect or title. Vlad cannot play it, nor benefit from it when it's in play.

Requires: Brujah antitribu.
Only usable by Brujah antitribu.

> blackday wrote:
> Im kinda confused and would like to know the explanation for the answer to these questions.
>
Nothing on Vlad's card text says he can meet a clan requirement, so he doesn't.

If the card requires a sect or title, he can meet the requirement to play it, if he himself plays it. e.g. Parity Shift, Kduva's Mask, Legacy of Power.

If a card is played by a Methuselah but not Vlad himself (e.g. master cards with a sect or title requirement), Vlad's cannot be used to meet those requirements. e.g. a vanilla Vlad cannot be used to play Temptation of Greater Power, because he doesn't play it himself, so it doesn't see him as a Justicar.

If a card requires a sect or title to play (whether minion or master), Vlad can use the card once it's in play as if he met the requirements of the in-play effects, if they're compatible. This is the "call a referendum to burn Purchase Pact" ruling. Purchase Pact requires a title to play, therefore once it's in play Vlad can "use cards requiring a title or a sect as if he had that title or were of that sect". So he can call the referendum to burn it - though he can't be used to meet the requirement to play Purchase Pact in the first place. It would also apply to, say, Powerbase Tshwane - you can't use him to play it, but since it does require a sect, he can use the built-in action to stealt it (which requires the same sect).

If a card doesn't require a sect or title to play, but has an in-play effect based on a particular sect or title, Vlad can't use that in-play effect. This is the Powerbase New York ruling. It would also apply to, say, Kaymakli Fragment's Sabbat level which has no requirement but has an in-play effect based on sect:

Requires: -
This Sabbat vampire may allow you to draw 5 cards from your library as an action (discard afterward).

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> blackday wrote:
> Just so i can explain why Vlad's ability is able to use the kduva mask and the abbot ability,was because that his ability read he may play and use any card that requires a sect/title?
>
First of all, does the card require a sect and/or title? If not, Vlad's special isn't relevant at all.

Then: if Vlad plays it (e.g. plays Parity Shift, plays War Party), the card sees him as meeting the requirement, for the usual play, resolution, and lingering effect. (This is how most other cards that let you play things "as if" something else work.)

However, if a card requires a sect and/or title, Vlad can also use it when it's in play as if he had the sect and/or title.

So:
Abbot
+1 stealth action. Requires a Sabbat vampire.
Put this card on this acting Sabbat vampire and untap him or her. This Sabbat vampire gets +1 intercept against  actions directed at his or her controller.

As a minion card played by Vlad that requires a sect and/or title, Vlad can play the card on himself, meeting the requirements using his special. Because the card requires a Sabbat vampire, Vlad can benefit from it as if he were a Sabbat vampire.

Legacy of Pander
Political Action
Requires a Sabbat vampire.
If this referendum is successful, put this card in play. Each non-titled Pander has 1 vote. Any Sabbat vampire may call a referendum to burn this card as a +1 stealth political action.

Similarly, Vlad can play LoP as if he met the requirements, using his special. Because it requires a Sabbat vampire to play, he may also use the in-play "call a referendum" effect as if he were a Sabbat vampire, using his special.

Purchase Pact, Master
Requires a ready archbishop, priscus, cardinal or regent.
Put this card into play. When a Sabbat vampire you control is in combat with another Sabbat vampire, you may tap this card before range is determined to end combat. Any titled Sabbat vampire may call a referendum to burn this card as a +1 stealth political action.

Purchase Pact is a master card, so Vlad doesn't play it. So for the purposes of playing Purchase Pact, Vlad's special is irrelevant. However, when a Purchase Pact is in play (yours or anyone else's), it is still a card that requires a title (from the first line). The in-play "call a referendum" effect is something that Vlad does, and since the card requires a title and/or sect, Vlad can use the in-play effect as if he had that title and/or sect. (The "tap this card" effect is used by the Methuselah, not Vlad.)

Powerbase: New York
Master: unique location.
Requires: nothing.
As a master phase action, you may burn 1 pool to move 3 blood counters from the blood bank to this card or move 1 blood counter from this card to your pool. Any Sabbat vampire controlled by another Methuselah can take a  action to move all the blood on the 'base to his or her controller's blood pool.

Powerbase: New York does not require a sect or title, therefore Vlad's special is irrelevant when playing it. The in-play effect requires a Sabbat vampire. However, Vlad can only use cards "as if" he had the sect and/or title if the card requires the sect and/or title. Since PB:NY doesn't require a Sabbat vampire to play it, Vlad can't use it as if he were a Sabbat vampire.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> blackday wrote:
> Regarding the closed session and private audience being played, am i right in the assumption it would lock down all votes by all vamps (inc. Vlad)except the political card played.
>
For clarity, the vote provided by the political action card isn't cast by a vampire. That goes to the Methuselah.  [DTR 19950509]

If you played Closed Session, then for its lingering effect, it will see Vlad as being a Sabbat Archbishop (or whatever title you chose). So it should allow him to vote.

If you play Private Audience, similarly, it will see Vlad as being a Camarilla Prince (or whatever title you chose) for its lingering effect. So it should allow him to vote.

The point about playing cards "as if" you met the requirements is that that card sees you as the impersonated requirements for play, resolution, and lingering effect. (But not effects that derive from the card going in play for most vampires - Vlad is different here.)

Votes can still be cast by Methuselahs, such as burning a political action card from hand, burning the Edge, tapping Ventrue HQ etc.

Note that there are earlier rulings to the contrary, but the "lingering effect" element of playing a card "as if" you were something was overturned in the  2007 RTR . And while it was originally phrased as affected allies, it was very quickly clarified to affect other "play as if" with a lingering effect, such as  Mata Hari + Raking Talons - RT sees Mata as a Gargoyle for its lingering effect, giving her agg hand damage, when previously it didn't.

Messages.Author: Borrelstein
Messages.Body:
Ok here is another funny one:

Will of the Council

[Action] Action

+1 stealth action. Requires a ready primogen.
Put this card on the acting primogen. During the referendum of a political action, this primogen can burn 1 blood to gain 1 vote. This primogen can burn this card to play a card that requires a prince as if he or she were a prince. This primogen can burn this card when a prince enters torpor to receive (and contest) the same title as that prince. A vampire can have only 1 Will of the Council.

So Vlad can play the card and use the ability to burn a blood for a vote. The ability to play a card as a prince is of course superfluous for him, but what will happen when a prince enters torpor? Can Vlad use the card ability to receive and contest the title, and what title will he then receive? Will he become a Camarilla once he starts the contest?

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Borrelstein wrote:
> what will happen when a prince enters torpor? Can Vlad use the card ability to receive and contest the title, and what title will he then receive?
>
Yes, he'll receive the title (there's a "but" coming up), and he'll receive the title that any normal Primogen would have received in that situation i.e. whatever the title on that Prince is.

+1 stealth action. Requires a ready primogen.
Put this card on the acting primogen. During the referendum of a political action, this primogen can burn 1 blood to gain 1 vote. This primogen can burn this card to play a card that requires a prince as if he or she were a prince. This primogen can burn this card when a prince enters torpor to receive (and contest) the same title as that prince. A vampire can have only 1 Will of the Council.

The card requires a title, so his special is relevant. When he uses the burn clause, he uses the card as if he were a Camarilla Primogen. So he gets the title.

Here comes the but...

> Borrelstein wrote:
> Will he become a Camarilla once he starts the contest?
>
No. Receiving a title doesn't make you the sect that title requires.

Having a Camarilla title while being non-Camarilla means that his title goes inert - he receives no benefit from it.

> Rulebook, wrote:
> If a vampire with a title changes clans or sects to a clan or sect inappropriate for his title, he loses the benefit of the title until his clan or sect changes appropriately. If he receives a new title, or if his title is contested (see Contested Titles, sec. 4.2), he immediately yields the old title.
>
And since he's going to contest it with the Prince, he immediately yields it.
